docs.title: ComputeAndTrackRoute
docs.text: Invokes the ComputeAndTrackRoute ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the nav2_route module. The server address can be remapped using the server_name input port.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Start pose. Optional. Only used if not left empty. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{start}".

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Goal pose. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{goal}".

docs.title: start_id
docs.text:
Type: unsigned int Default: N/A

Start node ID to use.

docs.title: goal_id
docs.text:
Type: unsigned int Default: N/A

Goal node ID to use.

docs.title: use_start
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false

Whether to use the start or use TF to obtain the robot's start pose.

docs.title: use_poses
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false

Whether to use the start and goal poses or start and goal node IDs.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, compute_and_track_route is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: execution_duration
docs.text:
Type: builtin_interfaces::msg::Duration Default: N/A

Time it took to compute the route.

docs.title: last_node_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

ID of the previous node.

docs.title: next_node_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

ID of the next node.

docs.title: current_edge_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

ID of the current edge.

docs.title: route
docs.text:
Type: nav2_msgs::msg::Route Default: N/A

List of RouteNodes to go from start to end.

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Path created by ComputeAndTrackRoute node.

docs.title: rerouted
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: N/A

Whether the plan has rerouted.

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Compute route error code. See ComputeAndTrackRoute action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<ComputeAndTrackRoute start="{start}" goal="{goal}" use_poses="{true}" use_start="{true}"
                      server_name="ComputeAndTrackRoute" server_timeout="10"
                      error_code_id="{compute_route_error_code}"/>

docs.title: ComputePathThroughPoses
docs.text: Invokes the ComputePathThroughPoses ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the nav2_planner module. The server address can be remapped using the server_name input port.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Start pose. Optional. Only used if not left empty. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{start}".

docs.title: goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

Goal poses. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{goals}".

docs.title: planner_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: ""

Mapped name to the planner plugin type to use, e.g. GridBased.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, compute_path_through_poses is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Path created by action server. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{path}".

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Compute path through poses error code. See ComputePathThroughPoses action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<ComputePathThroughPoses goals="{goals}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"
                         server_name="ComputePathThroughPoses" server_timeout="10"
                         error_code_id="{compute_path_error_code}"/>

docs.title: ComputePathToPose
docs.text: Invokes the ComputePathToPose ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the nav2_planner module. The server address can be remapped using the server_name input port.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Start pose. Optional. Used as the planner start pose instead of the current robot pose, if use_start is not false (i.e. not provided or set to true). Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{start}".

docs.title: use_start
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: N/A

Optional. For using or not using (i.e. ignoring) the provided start pose start. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{use_start}".

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Goal pose. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{goal}".

docs.title: planner_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: ""

Mapped name to the planner plugin type to use, e.g. GridBased.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, compute_path_to_pose is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Path created by action server. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{path}".

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Compute path to pose error code. See ComputePathToPose action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}" path="{path}" planner_id="GridBased"
                   server_name="ComputePathToPose" server_timeout="10"
                   error_code_id="{compute_path_error_code}"/>

docs.title: ComputeRoute
docs.text: Invokes the ComputeRoute ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the nav2_route module. The server address can be remapped using the server_name input port.

docs.title: start
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Start pose. Optional. Only used if not left empty. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{start}".

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Goal pose. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{goal}".

docs.title: start_id
docs.text:
Type: unsigned int Default: N/A

Start node ID to use.

docs.title: goal_id
docs.text:
Type: unsigned int Default: N/A

Goal node ID to use.

docs.title: use_start
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false

Whether to use the start or use TF to obtain the robot's start pose.

docs.title: use_poses
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false

Whether to use the start and goal poses or start and goal node IDs.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, compute_route is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: route
docs.text:
Type: nav2_msgs::msg::Route Default: N/A

Route created by action server. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{route}".

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Path created by action server. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{path}".

docs.title: planning_time
docs.text:
Type: builtin_interfaces::msg::Duration Default: N/A

Time it took to compute the route.

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Compute route error code. See ComputeRoute action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<ComputeRoute start="{start}" goal="{goal}" use_poses="{true}" use_start="{true}" path="{path}"
              server_name="ComputeRoute" server_timeout="10"
              error_code_id="{compute_route_error_code}"/>

docs.title: ConcatenatePaths
docs.text: Concatenates two paths into a single path, in order such that the output is input_path1 + input_path2. May be used with multiple of these calls sequentially to concatenate multiple paths.

docs.title: input_path1
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

First path to concatenate.

docs.title: input_path2
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Second path to concatenate.

docs.title: output_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Output concatenated path.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <ConcatenatePaths input_path1="{main_path}" input_path2="{last_mile_path}" output_path="{path}"/>

docs.title: ControllerSelector
docs.text:
It is used to select the Controller that will be used by the Controller server. It subscribes to the controller_selector topic to receive command messages with the name of the Controller to be used. It is commonly used before of the FollowPathAction. The selected_controller output port is passed to controller_id input port of the FollowPathAction. If none is provided on the topic, the default_controller is used.

Any publisher to this topic needs to be configured with some QoS defined as reliable and transient local.

docs.title: topic_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "controller_selector"

The name of the topic used to received select command messages. This is used to support multiple ControllerSelector nodes.

docs.title: default_controller
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The default value for the selected Controller if no message is received from the input topic.

docs.title: selected_controller
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The output selected Controller id. This selected_controller string is usually passed to the FollowPath behavior via the controller_id input port.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<ControllerSelector selected_controller="{selected_controller}" default_controller="FollowPath"
                    topic_name="controller_selector"/>

docs.title: DockRobot
docs.text:
Invokes the DockRobot ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the docking server.

It is used to dock the robot to a docking station.

docs.title: use_dock_id
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: true

Whether to use the dock's ID or dock pose fields.

docs.title: dock_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Dock ID or name to use.

docs.title: dock_pose
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

The dock pose, if not using dock id.

docs.title: dock_type
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The dock plugin type, if using dock pose.

docs.title: max_staging_time
docs.text:
Type: float Default: 1000.0

Maximum time to navigate to the staging pose.

docs.title: navigate_to_staging_pose
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: true

Whether to autonomously navigate to staging pose.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, dock_robot is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: success
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: N/A

If the action was successful.

docs.title: num_retries
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The number of retries executed.

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Dock robot error code. See DockRobot action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <DockRobot dock_id="{dock_id}" error_code_id="{dock_error_code}"/>

docs.title: DriveOnHeading
docs.text: Invokes the DriveOnHeading ROS 2 action server, which causes the robot to drive on the current heading by a specific displacement. It performs a linear translation by a given distance. The nav2_behaviors module implements the DriveOnHeading action server.

docs.title: dist_to_travel
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.15

Distance to travel (m).

docs.title: speed
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.025

Speed at which to travel (m/s).

docs.title: time_allowance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 10.0

Time to invoke behavior for, if exceeds considers it a stuck condition or failure case (seconds).

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, drive_on_heading is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Drive on heading error code. See DriveOnHeading action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<DriveOnHeading dist_to_travel="0.2" speed="0.05"
                server_name="backup_server" server_timeout="10"
                error_code_id="{drive_on_heading_error_code}"/>

docs.title: FollowPath
docs.text: Invokes the FollowPath ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the controller plugin modules loaded. The server address can be remapped using the server_name input port.

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Takes in a blackboard variable containing the path to follow, eg. "{path}".

docs.title: controller_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Mapped name of the controller plugin type to use, e.g. FollowPath.

docs.title: goal_checker_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Mapped name of the goal checker plugin type to use, e.g. SimpleGoalChecker.

docs.title: progress_checker_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Mapped name of the progress checker plugin type to use, e.g. SimpleProgressChecker.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, follow_path is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Follow path error code. See FollowPath action for the enumerated set of error code definitions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<FollowPath path="{path}" controller_id="FollowPath"
            goal_checker_id="precise_goal_checker"
            server_name="FollowPath" server_timeout="10"
            error_code_id="{follow_path_error_code}"/>

docs.title: GetCurrentPose
docs.text: Obtains the current pose from TF and places it on the blackboard for other nodes to use.

docs.title: robot_base_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Robot base frame to transform poses to if not given in the same frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's base_frame parameter value (base_link by default).

docs.title: global_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Global frame to transform poses to if not given in the same frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's global_frame parameter value (map by default).

docs.title: current_pose
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

The current pose in the global frame.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <GetCurrentPose current_pose="{current_pose}"/>

docs.title: GetPoseFromPath
docs.text: Gets a pose from a particular index on the path. Use -1 to get the last pose, -2 for second to last, and so on.

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Path to extract pose from.

docs.title: index
docs.text:
Type: int Default: 0

Index from path to use. Use -1 to get the last pose, -2 for second to last, and so on.

docs.title: pose
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Pose from path, with the Path's set header.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <GetPoseFromPath path="{path}" index="-1" pose="{goal}"/>

docs.title: GoalCheckerSelector
docs.text:
It is used to select the GoalChecker that will be used by the goal_checker server. It subscribes to the goal_checker_selector topic to receive command messages with the name of the GoalChecker to be used. It is commonly used before of the FollowPathAction. The selected_goal_checker output port is passed to goal_checker_id input port of the FollowPathAction. If none is provided on the topic, the default_goal_checker is used.

Any publisher to this topic needs to be configured with some QoS defined as reliable and transient local.

docs.title: topic_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "goal_checker_selector"

The name of the topic used to received select command messages. This is used to support multiple GoalCheckerSelector nodes.

docs.title: default_goal_checker
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The default value for the selected GoalChecker if no message is received from the input topic.

docs.title: selected_goal_checker
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The output selected GoalChecker id. This selected_goal_checker string is usually passed to the FollowPath behavior via the goal_checker_id input port.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<GoalCheckerSelector selected_goal_checker="{selected_goal_checker}"
                     default_goal_checker="precise_goal_checker" topic_name="goal_checker_selector"/>

docs.title: NavigateThroughPoses
docs.text: Invokes the NavigateThroughPoses ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the bt_navigator module.

docs.title: goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

Goal poses. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{goals}".

docs.title: behavior_tree
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Behavior tree absolute path. If none is specified, NavigateThroughPoses action server uses a default behavior tree.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, navigate_through_poses is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The lowest error code in the list of the error_code_names parameter.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<NavigateThroughPoses goals="{goals}" server_name="NavigateThroughPoses" server_timeout="10"
                      error_code_id="{navigate_through_poses_error_code}"
                      behavior_tree="<some-path>/behavior_trees/navigate_through_poses_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml"/>

docs.title: NavigateToPose
docs.text: Invokes the NavigateToPose ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the bt_navigator module.

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Takes in a blackboard variable containing the goal, eg. "{goal}".

docs.title: behavior_tree
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Behavior tree absolute path. If none is specified, NavigateToPose action server uses a default behavior tree.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, navigate_to_pose is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The lowest error code in the list of the error_code_names parameter.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<NavigateToPose goal="{goal}" server_name="NavigateToPose" server_timeout="10"
                error_code_id="{navigate_to_pose_error_code}"
                behavior_tree="<some-path>/behavior_trees/navigate_through_poses_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml"/>

docs.title: PlannerSelector
docs.text:
It is used to select the planner that will be used by the planner server. It subscribes to the planner_selector topic to receive command messages with the name of the planner to be used. It is commonly used before of the ComputePathToPoseAction. The selected_planner output port is passed to planner_id input port of the ComputePathToPoseAction. If none is provided on the topic, the default_planner is used.

Any publisher to this topic needs to be configured with some QoS defined as reliable and transient local.

docs.title: topic_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "planner_selector"

The name of the topic used to received select command messages. This is used to support multiple PlannerSelector nodes.

docs.title: default_planner
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The default value for the selected planner if no message is received from the input topic.

docs.title: selected_planner
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The output selected planner id. This selected_planner string is usually passed to the ComputePathToPose behavior via the planner_id input port.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<PlannerSelector selected_planner="{selected_planner}" default_planner="GridBased"
                 topic_name="planner_selector"/>

docs.title: ProgressCheckerSelector
docs.text:
It is used to select the ProgressChecker that will be used by the progress_checker server. It subscribes to the progress_checker_selector topic to receive command messages with the name of the ProgressChecker to be used. It is commonly used before of the FollowPathAction. The selected_progress_checker output port is passed to progress_checker_id input port of the FollowPathAction. If none is provided on the topic, the default_progress_checker is used.

Any publisher to this topic needs to be configured with some QoS defined as reliable and transient local.

docs.title: topic_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "progress_checker_selector"

The name of the topic used to received select command messages. This is used to support multiple ProgressCheckerSelector nodes.

docs.title: default_progress_checker
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The default value for the selected ProgressChecker if no message is received from the input topic.

docs.title: selected_progress_checker
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The output selected ProgressChecker id. This selected_progress_checker string is usually passed to the FollowPath behavior via the progress_checker_id input port.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<ProgressCheckerSelector selected_progress_checker="{selected_progress_checker}"
                         default_progress_checker="precise_progress_checker"
                         topic_name="progress_checker_selector"/>

docs.title: ReinitializeGlobalLocalization
docs.text: Used to trigger global relocalization using AMCL in case of severe delocalization or kidnapped robot problem.

docs.title: service_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Service name.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Service server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <ReinitializeGlobalLocalization service_name="reinitialize_global_localization"/>

docs.title: RemovePassedGoals
docs.text: Looks over the input port goals and removes any point that the robot is in close proximity to or has recently passed. This is used to cull goal points that have been passed from ComputePathThroughPoses to enable replanning to only the current task goals.

docs.title: radius
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.5

The radius (m) in proximity to the viapoint for the BT node to remove from the list as having passed.

docs.title: global_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Reference frame.

docs.title: robot_base_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Robot base frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's robot_base_frame parameter value (base_link by default).

docs.title: input_goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

A vector of goals to check if it passed any in the current iteration.

docs.title: output_goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

A vector of goals with goals removed in proximity to the robot.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <RemovePassedGoals radius="0.6" input_goals="{goals}" output_goals="{goals}"/>

docs.title: SmoothPath
docs.text: Invokes the SmoothPath action API in the smoother server to smooth a given path plan.

docs.title: unsmoothed_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The blackboard variable or hard-coded input path to smooth.

docs.title: max_smoothing_duration
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 3.0

Maximum time to smooth for (seconds).

docs.title: check_for_collisions
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false

Whether to check the output smoothed path for collisions.

docs.title: smoother_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The smoother plugin ID to use for smoothing in the smoother server.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, smooth_path is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: smoothed_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The output blackboard variable to assign the smoothed path to.

docs.title: smoothing_duration
docs.text:
Type: double Default: N/A

The actual duration used for smoothing.

docs.title: was_completed
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: N/A

Indicates if the smoothing process was completed. Will return false if check_for_collisions is set to true and a collision is detected.

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Follow smoother error code. See SmoothPath action for the enumerated set of error code definitions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<SmoothPath unsmoothed_path="{path}" smoothed_path="{path}" max_smoothing_duration="3.0"
            smoother_id="simple_smoother" check_for_collisions="false"
            smoothing_duration="{smoothing_duration_used}" was_completed="{smoothing_completed}"
            error_code_id="{smoothing_path_error_code}"/>

docs.title: SmootherSelector
docs.text:
It is used to select the Smoother that will be used by the Smoother server. It subscribes to the smoother_selector topic to receive command messages with the name of the Smoother to be used. It is commonly used before of the FollowPathAction. If none is provided on the topic, the default_smoother is used.

Any publisher to this topic needs to be configured with some QoS defined as reliable and transient local.

docs.title: topic_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "smoother_selector"

The name of the topic used to received select command messages. This is used to support multiple SmootherSelector nodes.

docs.title: default_smoother
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The default value for the selected Smoother if no message is received from the input topic.

docs.title: selected_smoother
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The output selected Smoother id.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<SmootherSelector selected_smoother="{selected_smoother}" default_smoother="SimpleSmoother"
                  topic_name="smoother_selector"/>

docs.title: Spin
docs.text: Invokes the Spin ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the nav2_behaviors module. It performs an in-place rotation by a given angle. This action is used in nav2 Behavior Trees as a recovery behavior.

docs.title: spin_dist
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.57

Spin distance (radians).

docs.title: time_allowance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 10.0

Time to invoke behavior for, if exceeds considers it a stuck condition or failure case (seconds).

docs.title: is_recovery
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: true

True if the action is being used as a recovery.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, spin is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Spin error code. See Spin action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<Spin spin_dist="1.57" server_name="spin"
      server_timeout="10" is_recovery="true"
      error_code_id="{spin_error_code}"/>

docs.title: TruncatePath
docs.text: A custom control node, which modifies a path making it shorter. It removes parts of the path closer than a distance to the goal pose. The resulting last pose of the path orientates the robot to the original goal pose.

docs.title: input_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The original path to be truncated.

docs.title: distance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

The distance to the original goal for truncating the path.

docs.title: output_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The resulting truncated path.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <TruncatePath distance="1.0" input_path="{path}" output_path="{truncated_path}"/>

docs.title: TruncatePathLocal
docs.text: A custom control node, which modifies a path making it shorter. It removes parts of the path which are more distant than specified forward/backward distance around robot

docs.title: input_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The original path to be truncated.

docs.title: distance_forward
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 8.0

The trimming distance in forward direction. Set to -1 to search full path forward.

docs.title: distance_backward
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 4.0

The trimming distance in backward direction.

docs.title: robot_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "base_link"

Robot base frame id.

docs.title: transform_tolerance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.2

Robot pose lookup tolerance.

docs.title: pose
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Manually specified pose to be used alternatively to current robot pose.

docs.title: angular_distance_weight
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.0

Weight of angular distance relative to positional distance when finding which path pose is closest to robot. Not applicable on paths without orientations assigned.

docs.title: max_robot_pose_search_dist
docs.text:
Type: double Default: numeric_limits<double>::infinity()

Maximum forward integrated distance along the path (starting from the last detected pose) to bound the search for the closest pose to the robot. When set to infinity (default), whole path is searched every time.

docs.title: output_path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The resulting truncated path.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<TruncatePathLocal input_path="{path}" output_path="{path_local}"
                   distance_forward="3.5" distance_backward="2.0" robot_frame="base_link"/>

docs.title: UndockRobot
docs.text:
Invokes the UndockRobot ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the docking server.

It is used to undock the robot from a docking station.

docs.title: dock_type
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

The dock plugin type, if not previous instance used for docking.

docs.title: max_undocking_time
docs.text:
Type: float Default: 30.0

Maximum time to get back to the staging pose.

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, undock_robot is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: success
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: N/A

If the action was successful.

docs.title: error_code_id
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

Dock robot error code. See UndockRobot action message for the enumerated set of error codes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <UndockRobot dock_type="{dock_type}" error_code_id={undock_error_code}/>

docs.title: Wait
docs.text: Invokes the Wait ROS 2 action server, which is implemented by the nav2_behaviors module. This action is used in nav2 Behavior Trees as a recovery behavior.

docs.title: wait_duration
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

Wait time (s).

docs.title: server_name
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Action server name. If not specified, wait is used.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Action server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <Wait wait_duration="1.0" server_name="wait_server" server_timeout="10"/>

docs.title: AreErrorCodesPresent
docs.text:
Checks the if the provided error code matches any error code within a set.

If the active error code is a match, the node returns SUCCESS. Otherwise, it returns FAILURE.

docs.title: error_code
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The active error code to compare against.

docs.title: error_codes_to_check
docs.text:
Type: vector<int> Default: N/A

The set of error codes you wish to compare against the active error code.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<!-- Error codes to check are defined in another port. -->
<AreErrorCodesPresent error_code="{error_code}" error_codes_to_check="{error_codes_to_check}"/>

<!-- Error codes to check are defined to be 101, 107 and 119. -->
<AreErrorCodesPresent error_code="{error_code}" error_codes_to_check="101;107;119"/>

docs.title: ArePosesNear
docs.text: Checks if two poses are nearby. If the input poses are in different frames, it will automatically transform both to the global frame.

docs.title: ref_pose
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Takes in a blackboard variable containing the initial pose to check.

docs.title: target_pose
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Takes in a blackboard variable containing the other pose to check against.

docs.title: global_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Global frame to transform poses to if not given in the same frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's global_frame parameter value (map by default).

docs.title: tolerance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.5

Tolerance to check poses if nearby with respect to.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <ArePosesNear ref_pose="{init_pose}" target_pose="{goal_pose}" tolerance="0.10"/>

docs.title: DistanceTraveled
docs.text: Node that returns success when a configurable distance has been traveled.

docs.title: transform_tolerance
docs.text: Defined and declared in Behavior-Tree Navigator.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
bt_navigator:
  ros__parameters:
    # other bt_navigator parameters
    transform_tolerance: 0.1

docs.title: distance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

The distance that must travel before returning success (m).

docs.title: global_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Reference frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's global_frame parameter value (map by default).

docs.title: robot_base_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Robot base frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's robot_base_frame parameter value (base_link by default).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <DistanceTraveled distance="0.8" global_frame="map" robot_base_frame="base_link"/>

docs.title: GlobalUpdatedGoal
docs.text:
Checks if the global navigation goal has changed in the blackboard. Returns failure if the goal is the same, if it changes, it returns success.

This node differs from the GoalUpdated by retaining the state of the current goal/goals throughout each tick of the BehaviorTree such that it will update on any "global" change to the goal.

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Destination to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goal}" if not specified.

docs.title: goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

Vector of goals to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goals}" if not specified.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <GlobalUpdatedGoal/>

docs.title: GoalReached
docs.text: Checks the distance to the goal, if the distance to goal is less than the pre-defined threshold, the tree returns SUCCESS, otherwise it returns FAILURE.

docs.title: transform_tolerance
docs.text: Defined and declared in Behavior-Tree Navigator.

docs.title: goal_reached_tol
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.25

Tolerance of accepting pose as the goal (m).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
bt_navigator:
  ros__parameters:
    # other bt_navigator parameters
    transform_tolerance: 0.1
    goal_reached_tol: 0.25

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Destination to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{goal}".

docs.title: global_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Reference frame.

docs.title: robot_base_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Robot base frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's robot_base_frame parameter value (base_link by default).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <GoalReached goal="{goal}" global_frame="map" robot_base_frame="base_link"/>

docs.title: GoalUpdated
docs.text: Checks if the global navigation goal, or a vector of goals, has changed in the blackboard. Returns failure if the goal is the same, if it changes, it returns success.

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Destination to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goal}" if not specified.

docs.title: goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

Vector of goals to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goals}" if not specified.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <GoalUpdated/>

docs.title: InitialPoseReceived
docs.text: Node that returns success when the initial pose is sent to AMCL via /initial_pose.

docs.title: initial_pose_received
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: N/A

Success if the value in the port is true. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{initial_pose_received}" if not specified.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <InitialPoseReceived/>

docs.title: IsBatteryCharging
docs.text: Checks if the battery is charging by subscribing to a sensor_msgs/BatteryState topic and checking if the power_supply_status is POWER_SUPPLY_STATUS_CHARGING. Returns SUCCESS in that case, FAILURE otherwise.

docs.title: battery_topic
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "/battery_status"

Topic for battery info.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <IsBatteryCharging battery_topic="/battery_status"/>

docs.title: IsBatteryLow
docs.text: Checks if battery is low by subscribing to a sensor_msgs/BatteryState topic and checking if battery percentage/voltage is below a specified minimum value. By default percentage (in range 0 to 1) is used to check for low battery. Set the is_voltage parameter to true to use voltage. Returns SUCCESS when battery percentage/voltage is lower than the specified value, FAILURE otherwise.

docs.title: min_battery
docs.text:
Type: double Default: N/A

Min battery percentage or voltage before triggering.

docs.title: battery_topic
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "/battery_status"

Topic for battery info.

docs.title: is_voltage
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: false

If true voltage will be used to check for low battery.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <IsBatteryLow min_battery="0.5" battery_topic="/battery_status" is_voltage="false"/>

docs.title: IsPathValid
docs.text: Checks to see if the global path is valid. If there is an obstacle along the path, it returns FAILURE, otherwise it returns SUCCESS. Optionally checks specific costmap layers and can use a custom footprint for validation.

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

The global path to check for validity.

docs.title: server_timeout
docs.text:
Type: chrono::milliseconds Default: N/A

Service server timeout (ms). If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's default_server_timeout parameter value (20 ms by default).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <IsPathValid server_timeout="10" path="{path}"/>

docs.title: IsStuck
docs.text: Determines if the robot is not progressing towards the goal. If the robot is stuck and not progressing, the condition returns SUCCESS, otherwise it returns FAILURE.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <IsStuck/>

docs.title: PathExpiringTimer
docs.text: Checks if the timer has expired. Returns success if the timer has expired, otherwise it returns failure. The timer will reset if the path gets updated.

docs.title: seconds
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

Time to check if expired.

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Check if path has been updated to enable timer reset.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <PathExpiringTimer seconds="15" path="{path}"/>

docs.title: TimeExpired
docs.text: Node that returns success when a time duration has passed

docs.title: seconds
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

The time passed to return success (s).

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <TimeExpired seconds="1.0"/>

docs.title: TransformAvailable
docs.text: Checks if a TF transform is available. Returns failure if it cannot be found. Once found, it will always return success. Useful for initial condition checks.

docs.title: child
docs.text:
Type: string Default: ""

Child frame for transform.

docs.title: parent
docs.text:
Type: string Default: ""

Parent frame for transform.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <TransformAvailable parent="odom" child="base_link"/>

docs.title: WouldAControllerRecoveryHelp
docs.text:
Checks if the active controller server error code is UNKNOWN, PATIENCE_EXCEEDED, FAILED_TO_MAKE_PROGRESS, or NO_VALID_CONTROL.

If the active error code is a match, the node returns SUCCESS. Otherwise, it returns FAILURE.

docs.title: error_code
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The active error code to compare against. This should match the controller server error code.

docs.title: error_codes_to_check
docs.text:
Type: vector<int> Default: N/A

The set of controller server error codes you wish to compare against the active error code.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <WouldAControllerRecoveryHelp error_code="{follow_path_error_code}"/>

docs.title: WouldAPlannerRecoveryHelp
docs.text:
Checks if the active planner server error code is UNKNOWN, NO_VALID_PATH, or TIMEOUT.

If the active error code is a match, the node returns SUCCESS. Otherwise, it returns FAILURE.

docs.title: error_code
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The active error code to compare against. This should match the planner server error code.

docs.title: error_codes_to_check
docs.text:
Type: vector<int> Default: N/A

The set of planner server error codes you wish to compare against the active error code.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <WouldAPlannerRecoveryHelp error_code="{compute_path_to_pose_error_code}"/>

docs.title: WouldASmootherRecoveryHelp
docs.text:
Checks if the active smoother server error code is UNKNOWN, TIMEOUT, FAILED_TO_SMOOTH_PATH, or SMOOTHED_PATH_IN_COLLISION.

If the active error code is a match, the node returns SUCCESS. Otherwise, it returns FAILURE.

docs.title: error_code
docs.text:
Type: uint16 Default: N/A

The active error code to compare against. This should match the smoother server error code.

docs.title: error_codes_to_check
docs.text:
Type: vector<int> Default: N/A

The set of smoother server error codes you wish to compare against the active error code.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: <WouldASmootherRecoveryHelp error_code="{smoother_error_code}"/>

docs.title: PipelineSequence
docs.text: Ticks the first child till it succeeds, then ticks the first and second children till the second one succeeds. It then ticks the first, second, and third children until the third succeeds, and so on, and so on. If at any time a child returns RUNNING, that doesn't change the behavior. If at any time a child returns FAILURE, that stops all children and returns FAILURE overall.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<PipelineSequence>
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</PipelineSequence>

docs.title: RecoveryNode
docs.text: The RecoveryNode is a control flow node with two children. It returns SUCCESS if and only if the first child returns SUCCESS. The second child will be executed only if the first child returns FAILURE. If the second child SUCCEEDS, then the first child will be executed again. If the second child returns FAILURE, the RecoveryNode returns FAILURE as well. The user can specify how many times the recovery actions should be taken before returning FAILURE. In nav2, the RecoveryNode is included in Behavior Trees to implement recovery actions upon failures.

docs.title: number_of_retries
docs.text:
Type: int Default: 1

Number of retries.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<RecoveryNode number_of_retries="1">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</RecoveryNode>

docs.title: RoundRobin
docs.text: Custom control flow node used to create a round-robin behavior for children BT nodes.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<RoundRobin>
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</RoundRobin>

docs.title: DistanceController
docs.text: A node that controls the tick rate for its child based on the distance traveled. The distance to be traveled before replanning can be supplied to the node as a parameter. The node returns RUNNING when it is not ticking its child. Currently, in the navigation stack, the DistanceController is used to adjust the rate at which the ComputePathToPose and GoalReached nodes are ticked.

docs.title: distance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

The distance travelled to trigger an action such as planning a path (m).

docs.title: global_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Reference frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's global_frame parameter value (map by default).

docs.title: robot_base_frame
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Robot base frame. If not provided, uses the BT Navigator's robot_base_frame parameter value (base_link by default).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<DistanceController distance="0.5" global_frame="map" robot_base_frame="base_link">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</DistanceController>

docs.title: GoalUpdatedController
docs.text: Checks if the global navigation goal, or a vector of goals, has changed in the blackboard. The node ticks its child if the goal was updated.

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Destination to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goal}" if not specified.

docs.title: goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

Vector of goals to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goals}" if not specified.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<GoalUpdatedController goal="{goal}" goals="{goals}">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</GoalUpdatedController>

docs.title: GoalUpdater
docs.text: A custom control node, which updates the goal pose. It subscribes to a topic in which it can receive an updated goal pose to use instead of the one commanded in action. It is useful for dynamic object following tasks.

docs.title: goal_updater_topic
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "goal_update"

The topic to receive the updated goal pose

docs.title: input_goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

The original goal pose.

docs.title: output_goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

The resulting updated goal. If no goal received by subscription, it will be the input_goal.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<GoalUpdater input_goal="{goal}" output_goal="{goal}">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</GoalUpdater>

docs.title: PathLongerOnApproach
docs.text: This node checks if the newly generated global path is significantly larger than the old global path in the user-defined robot's goal proximity and triggers their corresponding children. This allows users to enact special behaviors before a robot attempts to execute a path significantly longer than the prior path when close to a goal (e.g. going around an dynamic obstacle that may just need a few seconds to move out of the way).

docs.title: path
docs.text:
Type: nav_msgs::msg::Path Default: N/A

Path created by action server. Takes in a blackboard variable, e.g. "{path}".

docs.title: prox_len
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 3.0

Proximity length (m) for the path to be longer on approach.

docs.title: length_factor
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 2.0

Length multiplication factor to check if the path is significantly longer.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<PathLongerOnApproach path="{path}" prox_len="3.0" length_factor="2.0">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</PathLongerOnApproach>

docs.title: RateController
docs.text: A node that throttles the tick rate for its child. The tick rate can be supplied to the node as a parameter. The node returns RUNNING when it is not ticking its child. Currently, in the navigation stack, the RateController is used to adjust the rate at which the ComputePathToPose and GoalReached nodes are ticked.

docs.title: hz
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 10.0

Rate to throttle an action or a group of actions.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<RateController hz="1.0">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</RateController>

docs.title: SingleTrigger
docs.text: This node triggers its child only once and returns FAILURE for every succeeding tick.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<SingleTrigger>
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</SingleTrigger>

docs.title: SpeedController
docs.text: A node that controls the tick rate for its child based on current robot speed. The maximum and minimum replanning rates can be supplied to the node as parameters along with maximum and minimum speed. The node returns RUNNING when it is not ticking its child. Currently, in the navigation stack, the SpeedController is used to adjust the rate at which the ComputePathToPose and GoalReached nodes are ticked.

docs.title: min_rate
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.1

The minimum rate at which child node can be ticked (hz).

docs.title: max_rate
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 1.0

The maximum rate at which child node can be ticked (hz).

docs.title: min_speed
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.0

The minimum robot speed below which the child node is ticked at minimum rate (m/s).

docs.title: max_speed
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.5

The maximum robot speed above which the child node is ticked at maximum rate (m/s).

docs.title: goal
docs.text:
Type: geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped Default: N/A

Destination to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goal}" if not specified.

docs.title: goals
docs.text:
Type: vector<geometry_msgs::msg::PoseStamped> Default: N/A

Vector of goals to check. Takes in a blackboard variable, "{goals}" if not specified.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
<SpeedController min_rate="0.1" max_rate="1.0" min_speed="0.0" max_speed="0.5">
    <!--Add tree components here-->
</SpeedController>

docs.title: Collision Monitor
docs.text:
Source code and README with design, explanations, and metrics can be found on Github.

The nav2_collision_monitor package contains nodes providing an additional level of robot safety, namely the Collision Monitor and the Collision Detector. The Collision Monitor is a node providing an additional level of robot safety. It performs several collision avoidance related tasks using incoming data from the sensors, bypassing the costmap and trajectory planners, to monitor for and prevent potential collisions at the emergency-stop level. The Collision Detector works similarly to the Collision Monitor, but does not affect the robot's velocity. It will only inform that data from the configured sources has been detected within the configured polygons via a message to a topic.

docs.title: Provided Nodes
docs.text:
The nodes listed below are inside the nav2_collision_monitor package. See the pages for individual configuration information.

  • Collision Monitor Node

    Detects and prevents imminent collisions by limiting velocity commands.

    Go

  • Collision Detector Node

    Reports detected collisions without modifying velocity commands.

    Go

docs.title: Collision Detector Node
docs.text:
The Collision Detector is a node similar to the Collision Monitor, so it is recommended to read the Using Collision Monitor tutorial first.

In some cases, the user may want to be informed about the detected obstacles without affecting the robot's velocity and instead take a different action within an external node. For example, the user may want to blink LEDs or sound an alarm when the robot is close to an obstacle. Another use case could be to detect data points in particular regions (e.g extremely close to the sensor) and warn of malfunctioning sensors. For this purpose, the Collision Detector node was introduced. It works similarly to the Collision Monitor, but does not affect the robot's velocity. It will only inform that data from the configured sources has been detected within the configured polygons via message to the collision_detector_state topic.

See the package's README for more information.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
Similarly to the Collision Monitor, the Collision Detector uses robot's relative polygons to define "zones". However, unlike the Collision Monitor that uses different behavior models, the Collision Detector does not use any of them and therefore the action_type should always be set to "none". If set to anything else, it will throw an error

The zones around the robot and the data sources are the same as for the Collision Monitor, with the exception of the footprint polygon, which is not supported by the Collision Detector.

docs.title: frequency
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 10.0

Frequency of the main loop that checks for detections.

docs.title: base_frame_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "base_footprint"

Robot base frame.

docs.title: odom_frame_id
docs.text:
Type: string Default: "odom"

Which frame to use for odometry.

docs.title: transform_tolerance
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 0.1

Time with which to post-date the transform that is published, to indicate that this transform is valid into the future.

docs.title: source_timeout
docs.text:
Type: double Default: 2.0

Maximum time interval in which source data is considered as valid. If no new data is received within this interval, an additional warning will be displayed. Setting source_timeout: 0.0 disables it. This parameter can be overridden per observation source.

docs.title: base_shift_correction
docs.text:
Type: bool Default: true

Whether to correct source data towards to base frame movement, considering the difference between current time and latest source time. If enabled, produces more accurate sources positioning in the robot base frame, at the cost of slower performance. This will cause average delays for ~1/(2*odom_rate) per each cmd_vel calculation cycle. However, disabling this option for better performance is not recommended for the fast moving robots, where during the typical rate of data sources, robot could move unacceptably far. Thus reasonable odometry rates are recommended (~100 hz).

docs.title: polygons
docs.text:
Type: vector<string> Default: N/A

List of zones to check for data points. Causes an error, if not specialized.

docs.title: observation_sources
docs.text:
Type: vector<string> Default: N/A

List of data sources (laser scanners, pointclouds, etc...). Causes an error, if not specialized.

docs.title: Polygons parameters
docs.text: <polygon name> is the corresponding polygon name ID selected for this type.

docs.title: <polygon_name>.type
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Type of polygon shape. Available values are "polygon", "circle". Causes an error, if not specialized.

docs.title: <polygon_name>.points
docs.text:
Type: string Default: N/A

Here is an example of configuration YAML for the Collision Detector.

collision_detector:

      type: "polygon"

      source_timeout: 0.2
